title: The Mystery of the Water-Flowing Stone Garden
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Detective Yokomizo) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved, sharing an `order` integer so edges belonging to the same real occurrence can be grouped without a reifying node. The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep282-283...) had the correct culprit (Tomonori Kiyama) but understated the backstory: it described the deaths of the previous director and driver as a generic 'causes the deaths...in a cliffside car crash', when the transcript is explicit that Majima deliberately sabotaged the brakes to murder his predecessor and seize the company -- a real backstory murder, not an accident, and the true motive for both Kiyama's and Ayaka's revenge/investigation arcs. The old file also said Kiyama 'strangles' Majima; the post-mortem in the transcript states death was instant from a snapped neck, not strangulation. The old file omitted Ayaka Honjo (undercover as the housekeeper, secretly the murdered driver's daughter), the two false accusations Mouri Kogoro makes on-screen before the real solution (Hashimoto via an impossible rod-throw, then Endo via an archery-and-rope glide that the corpse's neat posture disproves), Endo's genuine but uncompleted plot against Majima (blackmail note + prepared archery rig, abandoned when Majima never arrived at the rooftop), and the conclusive fountain-pen-ink-stain clue that actually clinches the case against Kiyama. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: No footprints or drag marks around the body despite the freshly raked sand, yet marks are left on the rocks at the pool's edge -- shows the body was floated in and the mat dragged out, not carried across the sand.

The body was found lying face down with hands and legs neatly arranged, which is inconsistent with being dangled and dragged in on a rope as Mouri's archery theory required -- disproves that method and clears Endo of physically doing it.
The stain on the air mat is the same ink as Kiyama's father's fountain pen, the memento he always carries -- ties the mat directly to Kiyama rather than to whoever it was found sitting in his room.

Only the side of the body touching the ground was wet, and the rock garden is known to drain by ~9:00 PM -- together these fix the time and place of the killing to the fill/drain cycle, not a later dumping.

The exhibition ticket found stuck in the drain matches the ones Kiyama had been personally handing to guests that night, including Majima -- places Majima and Kiyama together shortly before the killing.
